- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#7 ("Follow-up after first results: sensitivity interval (P6), real-graph threshold explanation, (b) bias vs degree dispersion") by `experiment-repo`  > From `analysis`: the HK check (item 4) at the s = 0.5 level, from the block's exposure/dispersion tables (committed code; the CSVs go out with the export; the s = 0.25/0.75 rows and the paired intervals wait on the block-cells job, queued behind the GNN runs). Exploratory. Mechanism (d), Bernoulli p = 0.5, iid baseline, σ = 0.5, s = 0.5, regression (chin); bias in units of τ, log RMSE ratio to DM (>0: regression worse).
  > 
  > | graph | d=20 bias | d=20 log ratio | d=80 bias | d=80 log ratio | SD of exposure f at d=20 |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  > | WS | 0.775 | +0.47 | 0.232 | +0.06 | 0.112 |
  > | SBM (core / block) | 0.731 / 0.730 | +0.41 | 0.250 / 0.240 | +0.03 | 0.114 |
  > | ER | 0.737 | +0.42 | 0.267 | +0.01 | 0.115 |
  > | BA | 0.684 | +0.34 | 0.511 | +0.27 | 0.130 |
  > | **HK** | **0.671** | **+0.33** | **0.534** | **+0.33** | 0.132 |
  > | LN (log-normal degrees, no clustering) | 0.330 | −0.35 | 0.538 | +0.18 | 0.184 |
  > | ego-Facebook | 0.248 | −0.62 | — | — | 0.203 |
  > | Stanford3 | 0.197 | −0.89 | 0.176 | −0.96 | 0.209 |
  > 
  > Reading: **HK behaves like BA, not like the real graphs** (d=20: 0.67 vs 0.68 vs 0.20–0.25; log ratio +0.33 vs +0.34 vs −0.6…−0.9; d=80 also like BA, both above SBM). So tail + clustering together does not reproduce the real-graph result, and the two-factor reading gains no support; the cause stays open. What does track the d=20 bias is the spread of the exposure f: over the 9 graphs the Spearman correlation of SD(f) with bias is −0.95 (with log ratio −0.93) — LN, which has the many low-degree units but no clustering, goes about half-way (0.33, ratio −0.35). That is a description over 9 graph families (one run each, not independent draws), not a test; it is a different quantity from "degree tail" or "clustering" (HK has a higher degree CV² than LN, 1.68 vs 1.48, but a narrower f). At d=80 there is no such ordering (Spearman +0.21, n=7): BA/HK/LN sit at 0.51–0.54 while SBM/ER/WS sit at 0.23–0.27, Stanford3 at 0.18. I would word it as: clustering alone (WS) and degree tail alone (BA) and the two together (HK) do not reproduce the real-graph behaviour at d=20; a wide exposure spread goes with it; cause not diagnosed.
  > 
  > Also from the block, for the (b) condition: the tree-like form s·[HM/AM − 1] predicts the realised (b) bias on the new families without refitting: HK −0.141/−0.163/−0.129 predicted vs −0.147/−0.164/−0.127 realised (d = 20/5/80, p = 0.5); LN −0.311/−0.278/−0.305 vs −0.314/−0.274/−0.311; block SBM −0.024/−0.114/−0.004 vs −0.022/−0.113/−0.008. And "falls with d" does not hold for HK (−0.164→−0.147→−0.127) or LN (−0.27→−0.31→−0.31): consistent with the near-Poisson condition already in the Brief.
